A flood of excess can overwhelm rather than help.

semantic_axes.description: A surplus is an extra amount beyond current need; a surfeit is so much excess that it becomes unwelcome or burdensome.

edges.boundary_rule: A surplus is an extra amount beyond current need; a surfeit is so much excess that it becomes unwelcome or burdensome.
clues_b: spare stock earmarked for future needs

misconceptions.M1: Having extra stock does not mean it has become too much to use.
misconceptions.M2: A flood of excess can overwhelm rather than help.
misconceptions.M3: Do not stick with an old answer after decisive evidence changes, or let surface distractions override the boundary.

chains.frame: Which word best describes the lunch boxes Eleni had left?

beats.text: Eleni counted twelve extra lunch boxes after everyone had eaten; the staff refrigerated them for tomorrow.
beats.reason: The extras can serve a later need.

beats.text: She wrote the date on each lid.
beats.reason: Dating the lids changes nothing about their usefulness as extra stock.

chains.feedback_short: The key is usable meals beyond today’s needs; dating the lids changes nothing about their usefulness as extra stock.
chains.feedback_deep: Surfeit concerns unwelcome or overwhelming excess; surplus concerns usable extra beyond current requirements. Dating the lids changes nothing about their usefulness as extra stock.
chains.contrast_rule: Surfeit: an overwhelming number of options; surplus: useful extra supplies.

beats.text: Omar put out nine huge cakes for twelve guests, and almost everyone stopped eating after one slice.
beats.decisive_clue: a hugely excessive amount that guests cannot finish

beats.text: By evening, the untouched cakes occupied the entire fridge, leaving no space for dinner.
beats.decisive_clue: a hugely excessive amount overwhelming storage
beats.reason: The storage problem makes the unwelcome excess unmistakable.

chains.frame: Which word best describes the praise Felix received?

beats.text: Felix received hours of glowing praise after completing a tiny errand, until he began avoiding anyone offering more.
beats.decisive_clue: unwelcome excess of praise that drives him away
beats.reason: The excessive praise has made ordinary attention unpleasant.

beats.text: Several admirers continued praising him at length for the same small deed.
beats.decisive_clue: unwelcome excess of praise that drives him away
beats.reason: The continued, disproportionate praise reinforces that the attention is excessive and unwelcome.

chains.feedback_short: The key is unwelcome excess of praise that drives him away; continued disproportionate praise reinforces the same boundary.
chains.feedback_deep: Surfeit concerns unwelcome or overwhelming excess; surplus concerns usable extra beyond current requirements. Continued, disproportionate praise for a minor deed remains an unwelcome excess.
